newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA TO BACK FLOODLIGHT TESTS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA TO BACK FLOODLIGHT TESTS.

text.p: Tests between Australia and South Africa later this year could be played under floodlights if cricket's world ruling body gives the go-ahead.
The United Cricket Board of South Africa (UCBSA) is to back an Australian proposal to allow tests under lights, it was announced on Monday.

Ali Bacher, the UCBSA managing director, told a news conference it would fully support the Australian Cricket Board (ACB) which is to table the motion at an International Cricket Council (ICC) meeting in London next week.
Bacher said: "The ACB proposal comes as a direct result of experiencing first-class cricket under floodlights in South Africa earlier this year".
Mark Taylor's Australian team played tour games in Cape Town and Newlands where floodlights were turned on as a result of bad light.

Bacher said: "If the ICC gives the go-ahead to turning on the lights in tests in the event of bad light, the series between Australia and South Africa later this year could be the first to be played under the new dispensation".
South Africa are touring Australia starting in December.
